lead.headline: The Nasdaq-100 has its worst week since 2020, Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting inquiry, and Anthropic gives back half its gain
lead.short: The Nasdaq-100 fell 5.6% on Friday, ending its worst week since March 2020, and the S&P 500 fell 3.7% for a seventh straight day, pushing it and the Dow into a correction, 10% below their recent highs. Nvidia sank 14% after Reuters reported regulators were examining its accounting, and Anthropic's shares closed 8.5% lower.

why.text: Investors are doubting whether more than $1 trillion a year of AI spending will pay off, and the fall reached Bitcoin, metals and emerging markets.

more: "The problem stems from investors' rapidly changed perceptions about technology, particularly the pace and cost of the AI buildout," said Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers. A gauge of chipmakers fell 11%, and Wall Street's fear gauge rose to its highest since April 2025. Traders stopped fully pricing in a quarter-point Fed rate rise in December.

Anthropic's shares fell as much as 12% to about $85, close to their $83 listing price, after a 17% gain on Thursday. The BBC said the Democrats' midterm win had raised fears of tighter AI rules, while Nvidia and SpaceX faced problems of their own. Indian shares had a better day: the Sensex rose 1.1% on Friday to its highest close in three months.

seconds.headline: An Anthropic mathematician says he and Claude have proved the Riemann hypothesis, mathematics' most famous open problem
seconds.short: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he has found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis with the help of Claude, the company's AI model. "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," he wrote. "If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics," said the Fields medallist James Maynard.

why.text: If it holds, an AI-assisted proof would settle a problem that has defeated mathematicians since the 1800s.

more: The hypothesis, set out by Bernhard Riemann, who was born 200 years ago this September, concerns the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which encode how prime numbers are distributed. Riemann conjectured that, apart from some obvious cases, all of them lie on a single vertical line. If that is true, the primes are scattered among the whole numbers about as randomly as they could be.

Nature says a proof would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Riemann. The claim comes in a year in which AI has helped reach one mathematical breakthrough after another. Maynard is a number theorist at the University of Oxford. Alpöge works at Anthropic in San Francisco.

seconds.headline: COP31 talks in Turkey run into overtime as France, Panama and island states fight to keep fossil fuels in the deal
seconds.short: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey ran through Friday night in deadlock, as a group led by France and Panama pushed back against a draft agreement that made no reference to cutting the world's demand for fossil fuels. Producers led by Saudi Arabia had pushed for that language to be removed. A new, possibly final, text is expected on Saturday.

why.text: Without a fossil fuel commitment, the agreement would say nothing about the main cause of global warming.

more: "It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro. Spain, Belgium, Sweden and Finland joined the push. France's Monique Barbut attacked references to carbon capture as a licence for others to keep burning oil and gas.

Separately, the Africa Group is fighting for commitments on more money to help countries adapt to climate change, saying its members did not come to the summit "to beg". Europe says money already pledged should be used. The summit is being held in Antalya.

seconds.headline: At least 13 die and more than 300 are in hospital after drinking spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district
seconds.short: At least 13 people have died and more than 300 have been admitted to hospitals since 18 November after drinking spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, police said on Saturday. Most of the patients are from Chakpikarong and nearby areas and are being treated for suspected methanol poisoning at JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina hospitals in Imphal.

why.text: Hundreds of people in one district have been poisoned at once, and the toll may still rise.

more: "Thirteen people have been reported dead till 9 p.m. on Friday, while 346 patients have been admitted to hospitals due to suspected methanol poisoning," an official told PTI. More than 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and 41 to Babina Hospital. Some reports put the toll at 16 dead and 370 in hospital.

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija and Babina hospitals on Friday to see patients. The Chandel district administration has set up a team to coordinate the response, and four rapid response teams with medicines and oxygen have been sent to the district. Eleven of the deaths came in the 48 hours before Friday night, an official said.

stories.headline: Nikhil Gupta is sentenced to 19 years and seven months in the US for the plot to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
stories.short: A US federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 19 years and seven months in prison on Thursday for the failed plot to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a Khalistan separatist and American citizen, in New York. Gupta pleaded guilty in February and will be deported to India after his sentence. He apologised in court.

why.text: US prosecutors say he acted on the orders of an Indian government employee, a charge India has called "fabricated and malicious".

more: Prosecutors said Gupta was an "enthusiastic" participant acting on the directions of Vikash Yadav, then an employee of India's cabinet secretariat, which houses the Research and Analysis Wing. His lawyers argued he was only an intermediary with no previous criminal record. The sentencing had been postponed three times, and the hearing lasted nearly two hours.

Yadav has been on the FBI's most wanted list since October 2024. He was arrested in Delhi in a kidnapping and extortion case in December 2023 and given bail in April 2024, and his whereabouts are now unknown. Indian authorities had not commented on the sentence.

stories.headline: Trump says US companies will not be allowed to build AI data centres abroad, and threatens a "tremendous tax"
stories.short: Donald Trump said he would not allow American companies to build AI data centres outside the US, threatening a "tremendous tax" on those that do. "Because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen," he said after returning from Asia, adding that even his own officials were hearing the idea for the first time.

why.text: Meta, Google and other US firms have deals to build data centres abroad, and a ban would upend those plans.

more: He gave little detail, and it is unclear how such a ban would be enforced. "I don't know if that's a breaking story, but I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now, they're here," Trump told reporters. He said the US was leading the world in building data centres.

Data centres were a central issue in this month's midterms, when many Democrats promised tougher rules on building them. The idea follows Monday's rules requiring data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to get a US licence to buy advanced chips, aimed at stopping Chinese firms renting AI computing power.

stories.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over whether its chips reached China, as Huang agrees to a public Senate hearing
stories.short: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, has served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena over whether its advanced chips ended up in China and whether it misled investors. Jensen Huang has agreed to testify at a public US Senate hearing, an aide to Senator Tim Scott said, while Donald Trump called him "a good man" who deserves "a second chance".

why.text: Nvidia now faces state, congressional and reportedly federal scrutiny at once, while the president keeps pressing to bring its founder back.

more: "The conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said. Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is also examining Nvidia's accounting. Megaspeed, linked to Alice Huang, has bought nearly $5bn of Nvidia chips and hardware.

Scott's original request asked Huang to appear on 3 December, two days after a closed-door interview with three House committees. "I'd like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back," Trump said, adding that Xi had called Huang "brilliant", which contradicted Scott Bessent's account that Huang did not come up in Shenzhen. Nvidia's board has ruled out his return.

update.new: California subpoenas Nvidia; Huang agrees to a Senate hearing.

stories.headline: Alcaraz shrugs off his hamstring to beat Cobolli 6-4, 6-1, and plays Ben Shelton in today's ATP Finals semi-final
stories.short: Carlos Alcaraz beat Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 6-1 in 65 minutes in Turin on Friday, with strapping on his left thigh, to finish the group stage unbeaten. He hit 29 winners and did not face a break point. He plays Ben Shelton, whom he beat in last month's Paris Masters final, in the semi-finals at 19:00 IST on Saturday.

why.text: His scan did not stop him, and two more wins would give him the one big title he has never won.

more: "I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," he said. "The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow." He also wore tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm.

It was his 12th win in a row. Daniil Medvedev beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 to reach the semi-finals and will play Alexander Zverev in the other match. Alcaraz avoided sliding into the corners but still produced some astonishing shots, the BBC said.

update.new: He beats Cobolli despite the injury.

stories.headline: Antonelli is fastest in Las Vegas qualifying, but a five-place penalty hands Verstappen pole, with both Ferraris out in Q2
stories.short: Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but a five-place grid penalty means he starts sixth and Max Verstappen takes pole. George Russell, third fastest, starts second, beside the driver he clashed with in practice. Both Ferraris were knocked out in Q2, before the final shoot-out.

why.text: Russell and Verstappen, who have a long history of collisions, now share the front row after another row on track.

more: "It was certainly a strange qualifying session! I struggled to get the tyres into the right window," Antonelli said. He only just reached Q3 in tenth, then let the field pass him on his final run and crossed the line with about a second to spare before setting the fastest lap with help from the tow.

In practice, stewards found Verstappen had braked earlier than expected and changed direction under braking at Turn 14, and the two made contact as Russell passed him. "Somebody's got to stand up to that guy," Russell said. It was the second time in three weekends that Verstappen had been involved in a practice incident.
